svg.title: Shear force diagram and four candidate loading diagrams
svg.desc: The shear diagram begins at zero, falls to minus 40 kN over 2 m, jumps to plus 36 kN, stays constant for 1 m, drops to 16 kN, falls through zero after 1.6 m to minus 24 kN after another 2.4 m, jumps to 20 kN, then falls to zero over 2 m. Every loading option divides the beam into 2, 1, 4 and 2 m. A has 15 kN/m over the first 2 m and 10 kN/m over the last 6 m. B has 20 kN/m over the first 2 m, 15 kN/m over the next loaded 4 m and 10 kN/m over the last 2 m. C has 20 kN/m over the first 2 m and 10 kN/m over the last 6 m. A, B and C show an upward 76 kN at 2 m, downward 20 kN at 3 m and upward 44 kN at 7 m. D has the same distributed loads as C but downward 20 kN at 2 m and upward 76 kN at 3 m; its 44 kN upward force is at 7 m.
